        From ec3904a25562a105868163a69270ed79718ddb41 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: fertrist <fertrist@rambler.ru>
Date: Mon, 2 May 2016 13:34:44 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] fix "MIME" error introduced by commit
 a39de719e930f450c488dabd21f66f7221e5f80d

---
 src/main/java/org/mishpaha/project/config/SecurityConfig.java | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/main/java/org/mishpaha/project/config/SecurityConfig.java b/src/main/java/org/mishpaha/project/config/SecurityConfig.java
index a581a92..62e20fc 100644
--- a/src/main/java/org/mishpaha/project/config/SecurityConfig.java
+++ b/src/main/java/org/mishpaha/project/config/SecurityConfig.java
@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@ import org.springframework.security.web.csrf.HttpSessionCsrfTokenRepository;
 
 import javax.sql.DataSource;
 
-@EnableWebSecurity
+@Configuration
 @Order(SecurityProperties.ACCESS_OVERRIDE_ORDER)
 public class SecurityConfig extends WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter {
 
--

        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a misconfiguration in the security settings of the application, where the `@EnableWebSecurity` annotation was incorrectly used instead of the `@Configuration` annotation. This led to issues with the proper initialization of security configurations, resulting in a "MIME" error. The patch corrected this by replacing `@EnableWebSecurity` with `@Configuration`, ensuring that the security configuration is properly recognized and applied by the Spring framework.

The bug was caused by a misconfiguration in the security settings of the application, where the `@EnableWebSecurity` annotation was incorrectly used instead of the `@Configuration` annotation. This led to issues with the proper initialization of security configurations, resulting in a "MIME" error. The patch corrected this by replacing `@EnableWebSecurity` with `@Configuration`, ensuring that the security configuration is properly recognized and applied by the Spring framework.
